prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Houston, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1381; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just keep this to the accident itself, if that's okay.

Q: Understood. For the record, can you confirm you were the driver of the vehicle you were operating at the time of the collision?

A: Yes, I was driving my own car.

Q: Walk me through what happened at the intersection.

A: I was going through a green light heading east. A pickup coming from the north side ran the red and hit the passenger side of my car. I felt the impact right in the door area.

Q: Were you able to see the pickup before the impact?

A: Not really. It came out of nowhere. I think I had maybe half a second before it hit.

Q: Did you brake or swerve at all?

A: I tried to brake, but there wasn't time to do much. My car spun a little before it stopped.

Q: Did you hit your head or lose consciousness?

A: No, I didn't hit my head. I stayed awake the whole time.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: My neck is really stiff, and my lower back is aching. Turning my head to check traffic hurts. I went to urgent care that afternoon and they said it was a strain. I'm taking anti-inflammatories and I've been going to physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Have you had any prior neck or back problems?

A: Nothing serious. I had some soreness years ago after lifting something, but it went away and I didn't need treatment.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know?

A: Just that I'm still missing work because sitting and driving make the pain worse. I'd like to get this resolved.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
